markdown.markdown:
```{python} #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false import os import pandas as pd from IPython.display import display, HTML # Central bank current policy target benchmarks CURRENT_RATES = { 'FED': {'name': 'Federal Reserve (Fed)', 'rate': 5.25, 'file': 'data/fomc_curve.csv', 'link': 'rates_fed.html'}, 'ECB': {'name': 'European Central Bank (ECB)', 'rate': 3.50, 'file': 'data/ecb_curve.csv', 'link': 'rates_ecb.html'}, 'BOE': {'name': 'Bank of England (BoE)', 'rate': 3.75, 'file': 'data/boe_implied_curve.csv', 'link': 'rates_boe.html'}, 'BOJ': {'name': 'Bank of Japan (BoJ)', 'rate': 1.25, 'file': 'data/boj_implied_curve.csv', 'link': 'rates_boj.html'}, 'BOC': {'name': 'Bank of Canada (BoC)', 'rate': 2.25, 'file': 'data/boc_implied_curve.csv', 'link': 'rates_boc.html'}, 'RBA': {'name': 'Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA)', 'rate': 4.60, 'file': 'data/rba_implied_curve.csv', 'link': 'rates_rba.html'}, 'SNB': {'name': 'Swiss National Bank (SNB)', 'rate': 0.00, 'file': 'data/snb_implied_curve.csv', 'link': 'rates_snb.html'} } summary_rows = [] for key, meta in CURRENT_RATES.items(): if os.path.exists(meta['file']): df = pd.read_csv(meta['file']) if not df.empty: next_mtg = df.iloc[0] next_date = next_mtg.get('meeting_date', 'N/A') next_implied = next_mtg.get('implied_rate', 0.0) cur_rate = meta['rate'] change_bps = round((next_implied - cur_rate) * 100, 1) summary_rows.append({ 'Central Bank': f"{meta['name']}", 'Current Policy Rate': f"{cur_rate:.2f}%", 'Next Meeting Date': str(next_date), 'Next Implied Rate': f"{next_implied:.2f}%", 'Expected Move (bps)': f"{change_bps:+} bps" }) df_summary = pd.DataFrame(summary_rows) ``` Below is a live cross-market summary derived from our automated regularized WLS bootstrapping engines across global exchange-traded futures. ```{python} #| echo: false #| warning: false if not df_summary.empty: display(HTML(df_summary.to_html(escape=False, index=False, classes="table table-hover table-striped"))) else: print("Run the central bank engines to populate the summary table.") ``` ::: {.callout-note} ### Central Bank Models Hub Click on any central bank above or navigate via the **Rates** menu to explore individual meeting-by-meeting probability distributions, Markov chain step trees, and term structure paths. ::: --- ## Research & Publications *Quantitative macro notes, monetary policy transmission models, rate curve research, and correlations between short-term rates and trade financing.* ::: {.grid} ::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6} ::: {.card .h-100} ::: {.card-body}

Methodology Note

Unveiling the lagged and contemporaneous relationships between interest rate cycles and commodity inventories: using time-series analysis to measure how trade financing conditions impact metal inflows across the world's top trade hubs.
